subject: Opt-in telemetry implementation questions
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@brightmetrics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Opt-in telemetry implementation questions

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re moving forward with a proof-of-concept to wire the Redwood Console SDK into BrightMetrics for marketing analytics, but legal/privacy has a few implementation questions we need to clear before we start sending any telemetry:

1) Subprocessors: can you provide an up-to-date list of subprocessors (storage, analytics pipeline, BI)? Specifically we need to confirm any transfers outside the US/EU.

2) Data flow: attached is a simple diagram of the events we plan to send (telemetry_flow_v1.png). Can you confirm if event-level identifiers (session_id, anonymous_id) or any hashed PII would ever be forwarded to third-party partners?

3) DPA / SCCs: Redwood needs either a signed DPA with standard SCCs, or confirmation you can operate under Redwood’s DPA template. Do you support EU data residency for ingest or long-term storage?

4) SOC2 / security evidence: privacy asked for SOC2 Type II report or equivalent. Is there a secure share link you can provide?

5) Consent & opt-out: our site is first-party by default; we will only send telemetry once user opt-in is recorded. Can BrightMetrics accept an opt-in flag per event and not stitch across sessions when the opt-in is false?

If you can reply to the questions above (and drop links for subprocessor list + SOC2), I’ll loop in legal with a draft DPA. Happy to jump on a quick call if that’s easier.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Attachments: telemetry_flow_v1.png

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@brightmetrics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightMetrics Legal <legal@brightmetrics.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 12:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Opt-in telemetry implementation questions

Ben —

Appreciate the diagram — good clarity. Answers inline below.

1) Subprocessors: current subprocessors are: AWS (us-east-1 for compute), Google Cloud (BigQuery for analytics storage), Segment (for optional routing), and Sentry (error telemetry). Full CSV list + contact: https://brightmetrics.com/subprocessors.csv (public page). We do engage smaller EU-based partners for enrichment in specific customers; those are listed on the CSV.

2) Data flow: We do not require cleartext PII. Common fields we receive: event_name, timestamp, session_id (pseudonymous), anonymous_id, properties (customer-provided metadata). We only forward hashed identifiers if configured by customer integrations — otherwise we avoid cross-service enrichment. If you send an opt_in flag we can treat it as authoritative and disable stitching for opt-out events.

3) DPA / SCCs: BrightMetrics has a standard DPA and we can append SCCs on top. We also support EU-data residency options for storage in GCP eu-west-1 for an additional fee. We typically sign customer DPAs; if you send your DPA draft we’ll have Legal review.

4) SOC2: we can provide a read-only link to our SOC2 Type II report via secure ShareFile. I’ll have our legal team send the link to your legal contact.

5) Consent & opt-out: as noted, we can accept a per-event opt_in boolean and disable stitching when false. Please send the schema for the opt_in flag and we’ll validate on our side.

Happy to set a call if you want to walk through the schema.

Cheers,
Olivia Chen
Head of Integrations | BrightMetrics
olivia.chen@brightmetrics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 15:42:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Opt-in telemetry implementation questions

Ben —

Thanks for taking the lead. A few legal/privacy asks before we move forward with proof-of-concept traffic:

- Please request BrightMetrics to confirm the subprocessor CSV contains the contract-effective country and whether subprocessors can access event payloads in cleartext. EU cross-border transfer details should be explicit.

- We need to see the SOC2 Type II report and the scope (systems in-scope). A read-only link is fine but ensure the link is time-limited.

- For the DPA: Redwood will send our DPA template (attached). If BrightMetrics insists on their DPA, legal needs to mark up SCCs + data export controls. If they support eu-west-1 storage, get pricing and commitment.

- Implementation note: if BrightMetrics will disable stitching when opt_in=false, confirm how they treat historical data collected before opt-in and whether they will delete/expire it on request.

Once we have those confirmations we can sign-off on sending test events.

Marissa Cole
Legal Counsel, Privacy | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_dpa_draft_v2.docx
